reason: The hypothesis directly restates the known mechanism from P4, P7, P11, and P14: that segregation of Mn (and Ni, Cr) in CrMnFeCoNi leads to brittle intergranular precipitates and ductility loss at intermediate temperatures. The proposed intervention (thermal aging at ~700°C), the specific alloy, the precipitates (L10-NiMn, Cr-rich sigma), and the characterization methods are all taken from these passages. The only new element is the addition of cyclic mechanical loading, which is a minor modification and not justified by any new mechanistic insight or combination of sources.
copied_elements: grain-boundary segregation of a minor element (Mn) promotes brittle intergranular precipitates
L10-NiMn or Cr-rich sigma phases as the brittle precipitates
segregation reduces grain-boundary cohesion and toughness
TEM and APT to characterize grain-boundary precipitates
mechanical testing for ductility and toughness
